title: Power Pages: OpenID Connect sign-in accepts encrypted ID tokens
summary: Hold: saying the OpenID Connect governance control does not restrict encryption could mislead administrators about which sign-ins a protocol block prevents. Microsoft documents that blocking an authentication option prevents sign-in through that option; the briefing should distinguish this from the absence of an encryption-specific switch. The roadmap facts match, but the licensing field and abbreviated control paths also need clarification.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance control is reached at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > OpenID Connect > environment > Manage.
claims.quote: Under Authentication, select the authentication option you want to manage. Select an environment, and then select Manage. Choose the sites where makers can configure the authentication option.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > OpenID Connect > environment > Manage > site preference' and say the preference chooses all sites, all except selected sites, specific sites, or none. The cited operational page supports this route; the release-plan page https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/release-plan/2025wave2/power-pages/manage-external-authentication-provider-governance instead gives 'Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers', so retain the operational route and note that the release plan uses different labels.

claims.fix: Replace 'They restrict the OpenID Connect protocol, not encrypted tokens; Microsoft has not confirmed they apply to this feature.' with 'They govern OpenID Connect providers on targeted sites; this is a protocol control, not a documented encryption-specific switch.' Keep the prerelease qualification.

claims.where: Governance controls: final sentence; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The OpenID Connect governance control does not restrict encryption, and Learn does not say it governs token encryption.
claims.quote: When a governance setting that blocks an authentication option takes effect, users can no longer sign in or register by using that authentication option.
claims.fix: Replace 'It does not restrict encryption.' with 'This is a protocol control, not a documented encryption-specific switch; blocking OpenID Connect prevents sign-in through that protocol.' Replace 'Learn does not say it governs token encryption.' with 'Learn documents a protocol control, not an encryption-specific switch.' The control's documented reach includes OIDC sign-in regardless of token format, rather than permitting encrypted sign-in to bypass a protocol block.
